18. Capstone: a cause-of-death wide table

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-18-capstone.Rmd
book-18-capstone.Rmd

What you will learn

Combine ages, questionnaire answers, visit periods and causes in one private table, then use it to compare causes across age groups.

You need: the Opal login from Getting started, plus the date and category lessons. This chapter uses omop.questionnaire.

library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.questionnaire", server = "site")$conns

Find the concepts 

catalogue <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(900001L, 900002L, 900101L, 900102L,
  900201L, 900202L), conns = conns)$pooled
catalogue[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "domain_id")]
concept_id concept_name domain_id
900001 Education question Observation
900002 Fever question Observation
900101 Secondary education Meas Value
900102 University education Meas Value
900201 Myocardial infarction Condition
900202 Pneumonia Condition

The questions are Education 900001 and Fever 900002; answers Secondary 900101 and University 900102 are distinct from the questions. The coded causes are Myocardial infarction 900201 and Pneumonia 900202. Their occurrence was established in chapter 4.

Define one row per person

Keep people without visits, answers or deaths. Read the latest nonmissing answer from value_as_concept_id, and the cause from cause_concept_id. These definitions use all recorded history; the exercise below restricts education to before death.

education_event <- omop_event("observation", 900001L)
education <- omop_variable(event = education_event,
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
fever <- omop_variable(event = omop_event("observation", 900002L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
cause <- omop_variable(event = omop_event("death"),
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "cause_concept_id"))

Completed age uses the full birth date and the chosen anchor. An incomplete birth date or absent anchor gives missing age; it does not silently create a birthday. All calendar presentations below refer to the same first visit.

age_at_death <- omop_age_at("death")
first_visit <- omop_anchor(omop_event("visit_occurrence"), which = "first")
answer_keys <- c("concept:900101", "concept:900102")
variables <- list(
  age_at_death = age_at_death,
  age_band = omop_number_bins(age_at_death, breaks = c(0, 40, 121),
    labels = c("under 40", "40 and over")),
  age_at_first_visit = omop_age_at(first_visit),
  education = omop_category(education, omop_category_spec(levels = answer_keys,
    order = omop_category_order(c(answer_keys, "special:missing")), ordered = TRUE,
    missing = omop_category_missing(na = "level"))),
  fever = fever, cause = cause,
  visit_date = omop_date(first_visit),
  visit_month = omop_date(first_visit, omop_date_spec(precision = "month")),
  visit_quarter = omop_date(first_visit, omop_date_spec(precision = "quarter")),
  visit_year = omop_date(first_visit, omop_date_spec(precision = "year", representation = "number")))
capstone <- omop_recipe(variables = variables,
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
result <- recipe_execute(capstone, out = c(people = "D_capstone"), conns = conns)

The table stays on the server with a pseudonymous person key. Exact visit dates remain private; we use month and quarter categories for calendar counts.

Check age and missingness 

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_capstone$age_at_death",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_capstone$age_at_death
#> 32 33 42 43 NA
#>  6  6  6  6 24

Ages 32, 33, 42 and 43 each occur six times. The 24 missing ages combine 12 deaths with incomplete birth dates and 12 survivors. Missing age is not a fifth age band.

dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_capstone$age_at_first_visit", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 48
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean
#>   29   29   29   34   39   39   39   34
dsBaseClient::ds.numNA("D_capstone$age_at_first_visit", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] 24

There are 24 valid ages and 24 missing. The valid ages are 29 and 39, with a mean of 34 years. These describe the age at first care, not the later age at death.

Read the answers and calendar periods 

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_capstone$education",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_capstone$education
#>  Secondary education University education              Missing                   NA
#>                   12                   12                   24                    0
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_capstone$fever",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_capstone$fever
#> Yes  No  NA
#>  12  12  24

Education has 12 Secondary, 12 University and 24 Missing answers. Fever has 12 Yes, 12 No and 24 missing answers. No is an observed response; it is not a substitute for missingness.

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_capstone$visit_month",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_capstone$visit_month
#> 2020-03 2020-06 2020-07      NA
#>      12      12      12      12
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_capstone$visit_quarter",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_capstone$visit_quarter
#> 2020-Q1 2020-Q2 2020-Q3      NA
#>      12      12      12      12

March, June and July each contain 12 first visits, with 12 people lacking a visit. They fall in three different quarters, so changing precision leaves these counts unchanged. In other data, several months may merge into one quarter.

Use the table: cause by age at death 

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_capstone$cause",
  "D_capstone$age_band", useNA = "always",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
under 40 40 and over NA
Myocardial infarction 0 12 12
Pneumonia 12 0 0
NA 0 0 12

The 12 pneumonia deaths are under 40. Of 24 myocardial-infarction deaths, 12 are 40 or over and 12 have missing age. The 12 survivors have neither cause nor age at death. These are counts, not age-specific mortality rates: rates require age and person-time for survivors too, which the next chapter supplies. Fine cross-tabulations may be withheld when cells are too small; a withheld cell is not zero.

Exercises

1. Use only education recorded by death. Keep the same people and compare the education counts. Explain what happens to survivors.

Solution 1

before_death <- omop_variable(event = education_event,
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id",
    window = omop_window(NULL, 0, anchor = omop_anchor(omop_event("death"), which = "first"))))
restricted <- omop_recipe(variables = list(education = before_death))
recipe_execute(restricted, out = "D_before_death", conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_before_death$education",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_before_death$education
#>  Secondary education University education                   NA
#>                   12                   12                   24

The counts remain 12 Secondary, 12 University and 24 missing: all observed answers preceded death. This exercise uses the raw education variable without the category specification, so missing answers have the raw NA label instead of the main table’s “Missing”. A survivor has no death anchor, so this definition cannot supply an answer for that person. The unchanged totals do not make the window irrelevant.

2. Use year as a number. Find the mean first-visit year and its denominator. Then check how its type differs from the exact date and month category.

Solution 2

dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_capstone$visit_year", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 48
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean
#> 2020 2020 2020 2020 2020 2020 2020 2020
columns <- recipe_codebook(result)[[1]]$columns
columns[columns$name %in% c("visit_date", "visit_month", "visit_year"), c("name", "r_type")]
name r_type
visit_date Date
visit_month ordered_factor
visit_year integer

All 36 visitors have year 2020, so its mean is 2020; 12 people have no value. The codebook distinguishes Date, factor and numeric representations. Averaging calendar years is possible, but it cannot reveal the distribution across months.

Recap

One person-level table can combine answers, completed ages and calendar summaries. Its usefulness comes from a question answered with those columns, while retaining missingness and keeping patient rows private.
